newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says growth needed to boost revenue.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says growth needed to boost revenue.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Monday that stronger economic growth was needed to boost revenue and allow the government to fulfill its pledge to lower taxes.
When asked about the main problem in preparing the 1998 budget, Arthuis told Europe 1 radio more growth was needed.
"We need more growth to generate more revenues without having to raise taxes," he said. An early election would relieve uncertainty which he said was hampering investment and help to boost growth.

Arthuis' comments came amid mounting speculation that President Jacques Chirac would call an early general election on Monday evening to clear the way for France's preparations to qualify for membership in a single European currency.
Arthuis said the government needed a new five-year mandate.

He said its policies so far had been successful. "The proof is that growth is there. The proof is that interest rates have fallen to record lows," he said. "There is now a margin for manoeuvre which stems precisely from the fall in rates."
He said the government needed more time to carry out its programme. 1997, he said, "is year one of fiscal reform. It is year one of the cut in income taxes," he said.
